verified.coverageNote: 1516 new distinct JDK Double.parseDouble inputs extend the matrix to 31137 strings in 244 groups. Existing 2342 bounded JDK Integer inputs remain in 19 groups. Existing 1226 entry programs include 406 portable programs and repeat in async checks. Fifteen saved-native suites total 31776 runs, retaining historical overlaps. Existing 24254 Double render bit patterns remain. Full conformance is not established.
verified.api: Typed lists borrow the private input array while returning fresh converted results, without per-element singleton maps or path parsing. Element errors, Bare coercion and object deep copies remain. Decimal grammar scanning accumulates at most 16 significant digits, using one exact-operand floating operation only below 2^53 and within powers -22 through 22; all other paths remain.

performance.scope: Twelve exact-render workloads, sixteen existing workloads and six retained Double-list reads compare current, fixed 0.21 and native Config. Long coefficients retain the same exact bounded midpoint conversion as baseline. Three additional list reads cover 64 and 512 mixed ordinary values and 16 exact-operation candidates. Current performs direct element conversion and single-scan exact-operation decimal parsing; no per-input or per-path result caches are used. Double-list output is compared as exact binary64 bit strings, converted after timing; public getDoubleList calls and list construction occur inside timing. Render timers retain the prepared ConfigValue; Java retains options and JS constructs its options object inside each call and include returned text; source parsing, optional partial resolution and final result-array serialization are excluded. The full baseline JS module dependency tree is loaded from the fixed Git commit. Retained workloads compare real Config methods with native Config; construction excluded, immutable operations/getter transport included, final result serialization excluded. Each workload has five fresh processes; Java legacy and retained workloads use separate processes. Startup, I/O and sustained/peak-memory parity are not measured.
